---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation with a new owner to set up where recipes are
  stored and which units they prefer, then offer a sample recipe.
---
# Getting started

You turn any dish request into a ready-to-cook recipe workbook with scalable servings, a grocery list and source notes, saved where the owner wants it.

Talk like a friendly cook: short, plain, one question at a time. Start with a short hello, then:

1. **Where to store recipes.** Ask: Google Drive (a native Google Sheet; needs the Google Sheets and Google Drive connectors) or a local folder (an .xlsx file; ask for the folder path)? If they choose Google Drive and the connectors aren't connected yet, offer to connect them so the connect card appears, and ask which Drive folder to use (the Drive root is fine). If they choose local, ask for the exact folder path and confirm it exists. Save the answer to memory.
2. **Units.** Ask: US measurements (cups, Tbsp, tsp, fl oz, lb, oz, °F) or metric (grams, ml, liters, °C)? Save the answer to memory.
3. Tell them you'll reuse both answers silently on every future recipe until they ask to change them.
4. **Offer a sample recipe.** Ask what dish they'd like first (or suggest a simple one if they're unsure). If they name a dish, skip the question and start right away.

Then run the normal workflow for each request: ask the dish (skip if named, and only ask about servings, dietary needs or a preferred chef if it matters); find a well-regarded recipe from a reputable source (for example Serious Eats, America's Test Kitchen, King Arthur, Bon Appetit or a named chef) and keep the exact source text and link; build the three-tab workbook by following the recipe-workbook-format skill exactly (its layout, colors, merges, formulas, dish-photo rule and builder script are complete; do not look for any other reference); include a real photo of the finished dish when one is available (never a generated image); save it to the chosen place; and report the file name and a link or path. Never reply with chat text only. Do not send or share a recipe with anyone unless the owner asks.

skills.name: recipe-workbook-format
skills.description: Use when building any recipe workbook, either an Excel .xlsx or a native Google Sheet, in the standard three-tab format with scalable servings, vertical merged phase blocks, an optional real dish photo, grocery list and source text. Contains the full layout spec and a working openpyxl builder.
skills.content:
---
name: recipe-workbook-format
description: >-
  Use when building any recipe workbook, either an Excel .xlsx or a native
  Google Sheet, in the standard three-tab format with scalable servings,
  vertical merged phase blocks, an optional real dish photo, grocery list and
  source text. Contains the full layout spec and a working openpyxl builder.
---
# Recipe workbook format (complete spec, self-contained)

Every recipe is ONE workbook with exactly 3 tabs, in this order: `<Dish> Recipe Table`, `Grocery List`, `Source Notes – <Source>` (en dash). Excel tab names are max 31 characters, so shorten the dish part if needed and keep the full name in the titles. Never look anything up outside this spec for the layout.

## Global rules
- **Fonts:** Arial for every styled cell. Cells left unstyled (merged-range interiors, blank spacer cells, the cells to the right of a tip) keep the workbook default, Calibri 11.
- **Palette (hex):**
  - cream `FFFFCC` (title, scale row, banners, ingredient and phase cells)
  - mint `E2EFDA` (SERVINGS label, header rows, Key Tips)
  - input yellow `FFFF99`
  - dark green text `006600`
  - input blue text `0000FF`
  - grey note text `666666`
  - all other text uses the automatic color (black); never set an explicit black.
- **Borders:** thin, automatic color (black), on all four sides of every bordered cell (the `BOX` style). Where a bordered cell starts a merge, the merged range gets the same outline: middle cells of a horizontal merge get top and bottom, the last cell also gets right; a vertical merge gets left and right on every cell and bottom on the last. openpyxl's `merge_cells` does this automatically when the top-left cell already has `BOX`. Merged interior cells have no fill and no font of their own.
- **View:** gridlines ON (the default; never set `showGridLines`). No zoom setting, no tab colors. Freeze panes at `A8` on the Recipe Table only (7 rows frozen); none elsewhere.
- **Print:** none. No orientation, paper size, fit-to-page or print area on any tab. Margins are Excel's defaults: left/right 0.75, top/bottom 1.0, header/footer 0.5.
- **Labels:** use `SERVINGS` when the source states a yield. Use `BATCHES` when it doesn't, e.g. a dictated family recipe with no yield. The choice changes A2, C2, C3 (`" servings"` / `" batch(es)"`), the Key Tips line, the Grocery List row 2 label and the how-to line.
- **No hidden or helper columns:** all scaling math lives inside the column A formulas and the phase-block formulas.

## Tab 1: Recipe Table
**Columns:** A, then one column per phase (B, C, D, …). Use 4 phases when the method fits (that is the standard). Otherwise use 3, 5 or 6 in the same style. Let L be the last phase column (E for 4 phases).

**Widths (characters):** A 48. The first two phase columns are 16; every later phase column is 18. For 4 phases: A 48, B 16, C 16, D 18, E 18.

| Row | Content | Merge | Style | Height (pt) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `<Dish> – <Source> (<short descriptor>)`, about 60 characters so it stays on one line | A1:L1 | Arial 14 bold `006600`, cream, BOX, vertical center, wrap | 27.75 |
| 2 | A2 `SERVINGS` (or `BATCHES`) | – | Arial 11 bold `006600`, mint, BOX, no alignment | 18 |
| 2 | B2 the input number (the only input; deliver at the base amount unless asked) | – | Arial 14 bold `0000FF`, yellow `FFFF99`, BOX, vertical center | |
| 2 | C2 `← change this number (base recipe = N servings …)` | C2:L2 | Arial 9 `666666`, no fill, BOX, vertical center | |
| 3 | A3 `Scale factor` | – | Arial 10, cream, BOX, no alignment | default (not set) |
| 3 | B3 `=B2/N` (N = base servings or batches) | – | Arial 10 bold, cream, BOX | |
| 3 | C3 `=CONCATENATE("Currently scaled for ",B2," servings")` (or `" batch(es)"`) | C3:L3 | Arial 10, cream, BOX | |
| 4 | blank spacer | – | – | 7.5 |
| 5 | Overview banner (setup / prep summary, at most 2 lines, about 240 characters) | A5:L5 | Arial 10 bold, cream, BOX, vertical center, wrap | 31.5 |
| 6 | Cook/serve banner: a formula, `=IF(B3=1,"base text","Scaled to "&B2&" servings: …")` | A6:L6 | same as row 5 | 31.5 |
| 7 | A7 `INGREDIENT (auto-scales)`; B7… phase names (short, Title Case, e.g. `Mix Dry`, `Cut Butter`, `Combine`, `Drop & Bake`) | – | Arial 12 bold `006600`, mint, BOX, wrap, vertical center; phase headers also horizontally centered | 21.75 |
| 8…n | One row per ingredient (see below) | phase blocks | A: Arial 12, cream, BOX, vertical center, wrap. Phase cells: Arial 12 bold, cream, BOX, centered both ways, wrap | 31 |
| n+1 | blank spacer | – | – | 9.75 |
| n+2 | `KEY TIPS  •  Quantities above auto-scale when you change the SERVINGS number  •  Scale factor = B2/N` (keep it to about 100 characters) | A:L | Arial 12 bold `006600`, mint, NO border, vertical center, wrap | 24 |
| tips | one `• tip` per row, at most about 105 characters so it fits one line | A:L each | Arial 12, no fill, no border, vertical center, wrap | 18 |

### Ingredient rows and vertical phase blocks
- **Column A:** ONE text formula per ingredient: `=IF(B3=1,"<published text>",<scaled text>)`.
  - At scale 1 it shows the published wording exactly.
  - Non-scaling rows (salt to taste, equipment) hold literal text.
- **Row order:** list ingredients in order of first use.
- **Phase blocks:** each phase column holds exactly ONE instruction block, merged vertically. The block starts at the first ingredient row (row 8) and runs down to the last ingredient row that phase uses, so later phases make longer blocks. For example, with 6 ingredients, B8:B11, C8:C12, D8:D13, E8:E13. A phase whose last ingredient is row 8 is a single unmerged cell.
- **Block text:** short lowercase clauses separated by line breaks (`\n`, written as `CHAR(10)` in formulas).
  - Keep each line to about 13 characters in a 16-wide column and about 15 in an 18-wide column.
  - Keep the total line count under about 2 lines per row spanned at 31 pt, because Excel does not auto-fit merged cells.
  - When a block includes a scaled amount, make it a formula `=IF(B3=1,"base text","…"&<scaled amount>&"…")`.
- **Cells below a block:** phase cells under the end of a block stay empty but keep the cream fill, BOX border and Arial 12 bold.

### Dish photo (only when a real photo exists)
- **Source:** use a real photo of the finished dish only: the source post's or recipe page's photo, or one the owner sends. Never use a generated or AI image. If there is no real photo, leave the photo and caption out entirely (the layout is then exactly as above).
- **Placement:** embed it on the Recipe Table tab with `openpyxl.drawing.image.Image`, anchored at row 1 one column past an empty gap column to the right of the table (column L+2; `G1` for 4 phases). It must not overlap any table cell.
- **Size:** about 300 px wide, aspect ratio kept (height = original height × 300 / original width).
- **Caption:** one cell crediting the photo's source (e.g. `Photo: <account> / <site>`), Arial 9 grey `666666`, no fill, no border, in the same column just below the image's last row. Find that row by adding row heights from row 1 (points × 4/3 = pixels; unset rows are 15 pt) until the total reaches the image height; the caption goes in the next row.
- **Column width:** the photo column is 44 characters wide so the image and caption fit. The gap column keeps the default width.
- **Builder:** pass `photo` (file path) and `photo_credit` (caption text) in `R`. `recalc()` copies every zip part unchanged except the worksheet cell values, so the image and drawing parts survive; still verify that the delivered file contains `xl/media/` and `xl/drawings/` parts.

## Tab 2: Grocery List (columns A:C, widths 42 / 55 / 40)
- **Row 1:** `Grocery List – <Dish>`, merged A1:C1. Arial 14 bold `006600`, cream, no border, no alignment. Height 18.
- **Row 2:**
  - A2 `Servings (linked to main sheet):` (or `Batches (…)`), Arial 11, no fill.
  - B2 `='<Tab1>'!B2`, Arial 14 bold `0000FF` on yellow `FFFF99`, no border.
  - Height 18.
- **Row 3:** A3 `Scale factor:` and B3 `='<Tab1>'!B3`, both Arial 11, no fill. Default height.
- **Row 4:** blank, default height.
- **Row 5:** header `Item | Quantity (scaled) | Notes`. Arial 12 bold `006600`, mint, BOX, no alignment. Height 15.5.
- **Rows 6…:** one per grocery item, normally one per Recipe Table ingredient, plus any extra equipment.
  - A is the item name, B is `='<Tab1>'!A<row>` (or a literal quantity for non-scaling items, e.g. `1 sheet`, `To taste`), C is a short note (may be empty).
  - All three cells: Arial 10, no fill, BOX, vertical center, wrap, even when empty. Height 30.
- **Footer:** one blank row (default height), then two lines, each merged A:C, Arial 9, no fill, no border, wrap (no vertical alignment), height 24:
  - `How to use: Change the SERVINGS number on the '<Tab1>' sheet. All quantities here and on the main table update automatically via scale factor.`
  - `Base recipe = N servings (…). Scale factor = desired servings / N. …`

## Tab 3: Source Notes – <Source> (column A only, width 120, no merges)
- **Row 1:** `SOURCE TEXT – <Dish> (<source description>)`. Arial 14 bold `006600`, cream, no border, not merged, no alignment. Height 18.
- **Other rows:** default height (not set), Arial 10, no fill, no alignment and NO wrap, one line per row.
- **Bold lines:** rows 2–7 in this order: `Title:`, `Source:`, `Author:`, `Rating:` (only from the page or its structured data, never invented; write `Not specified` or `no rating shown` otherwise), `Prep Time / Cook Time:`, `Servings / Yield:`.
- **Sections:** after a blank row, bold labels `Ingredients (verbatim as published):` and `Steps (verbatim as published):`, plus a source notes or tips label if present. The last section is a `Notes:` label for the workbook's own notes: conversions, rounding, conflicts, assumptions, adaptations and the SERVINGS/BATCHES choice. Leave one blank row between sections.
- **Content lines:** plain (not bold). Ingredients and notes start with `• `, steps with `1. `, `2. `, and so on, with the text verbatim. With more than one source, repeat the sections per source with ` – <recipe name>` after the label.
- **Source URLs:** put them in the `Source:` line or in a final bold `Source URLs:` section.
- **Long lines:** because there is no wrap, a line longer than about 130 characters continues on the next row, indented three spaces, with the same boldness.

## Measurements, scaling and rounding (inline formulas)
- **Unit system:** the owner's remembered system comes first. US: cups, Tbsp, tsp, lb, oz, °F. Metric: g, ml, °C. The other system goes in parentheses, using published metric where given and approximate conversions otherwise (say so in Notes).
- **Rounding:** scaled amounts round to kitchen-friendly steps.
  - US steps: ¼ cup, ½ Tbsp, ½ tsp, ¼ lb, ½ oz, with floors of ⅛ cup, ¼ Tbsp, ⅛ tsp, ⅛ lb, ¼ oz so small amounts never become zero.
  - Teaspoons roll up: 3 tsp or more shows as Tbsp, to the nearest ½ Tbsp.
  - Counts are whole numbers, minimum 1.
  - Metric is whole g/ml, with 0.1 resolution under 1.
- **Display:** show fractions with unicode characters (⅛ ¼ ⅜ ½ ⅝ ¾ ⅞) and pluralize cups (`1 cup`, `1 ¼ cups`).
- **Base text:** at scale factor 1 show the published text exactly (`IF(B3=1, …)`). The base servings value lives in `=B2/N` and in the literal texts.
- **Source conflicts:** pick one value and note the conflict in Notes (and in a tip if it matters).
- **Formula length:** Excel formulas must stay under 8,000 characters.

## Excel build path (.xlsx, openpyxl + LibreOffice)
1. Save `rg_builder.py` (below) and write a recipe script like `example.py` (below) with the data block for the dish. Run `python3 recipe.py SERVINGS OUT.xlsx`.
2. `recalc()` computes cached values with LibreOffice headless and injects them into the openpyxl file. Deliver that file. Do NOT deliver a LibreOffice-saved copy: LibreOffice rewrites border colors, rounds row heights (31 → 30.75), writes explicit heights for default rows and adds a portrait A4 page setup.
3. Verify:
   - every formula cell has a cached value with no `#REF!`, `#NAME?`, `#VALUE!`, `#DIV/0!`, `#N/A` or `Err:`;
   - build temporary copies at 2 or more larger/smaller amounts and read back column A, the phase blocks and the Grocery List;
   - the merges, A8 freeze, gridlines, widths and heights match this spec;
   - with a photo: the file contains `xl/media/` and `xl/drawings/` parts, the caption sits in the row below the image, and the image does not overlap the table;
   - deliver at the base servings.
4. **Visual check:** convert a temporary copy to PDF with fit-to-page set only on that copy. Look for clipped phase blocks and headers (if a block overflows, shorten its lines), and, with a photo, check that the image sits right of the table without covering any cells.

### rg_builder.py (tested)
```python
# Recipe workbook builder (openpyxl). usage: from rg_builder import build; build(R, "out.xlsx")
import math
from openpyxl import Workbook
from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill, Alignment, Border, Side
from openpyxl.styles.colors import Color

CREAM, MINT, YEL, GREEN, BLUE, GREY = 'FFFFCC', 'E2EFDA', 'FFFF99', '006600', '0000FF', '666666'
def F(sz, b=False, color=None): return Font(name='Arial', size=sz, bold=b, color=color)   # color None = automatic (black)
def FILL(h): return PatternFill('solid', fgColor=h)
T = Side(style='thin', color=Color(auto=True)); BOX = Border(left=T, right=T, top=T, bottom=T)
VC = Alignment(vertical='center'); VCW = Alignment(vertical='center', wrap_text=True)
CCW = Alignment(horizontal='center', vertical='center', wrap_text=True); WR = Alignment(wrap_text=True)

def Q(s):   # Excel string literal; "\n" becomes CHAR(10)
    return '&CHAR(10)&'.join('"' + p.replace('"', '""') + '"' for p in s.split('\n'))

# ---- kitchen rounding, all inline (no helper columns). x = Excel expression of the scaled number
STEPS = {'cup': (0.25, 0.125), 'Tbsp': (0.5, 0.25), 'tsp': (0.5, 0.125), 'lb': (0.25, 0.125), 'oz': (0.5, 0.25)}  # (step, floor)
def kround(x, unit):
    if unit in ('g', 'ml'): return f'IF(({x})<1,MAX(0.1,ROUND({x},1)),ROUND({x},0))'
    a, f = STEPS[unit]
    return f'IF(({x})<{a},MAX({f},ROUND(({x})/{f},0)*{f}),ROUND(({x})/{a},0)*{a})'
def frac(e):  # number on a 1/8 grid -> "1 ¾"
    return (f'IF(INT({e})>0,INT({e})&IF({e}-INT({e})>0.001," ",""),"")&'
            f'CHOOSE(ROUND(({e}-INT({e}))*8,0)+1,"","⅛","¼","⅜","½","⅝","¾","⅞")')
def amt(q, unit):   # Excel text expression: scaled, rounded amount + unit
    k = kround(f'{q}*B3', unit)
    if unit in ('g', 'ml'): return f'ROUND({k},1)&" {unit}"'
    if unit == 'tsp':   # roll-up: 3 tsp or more shows as Tbsp (nearest ½ Tbsp)
        tb = f'(ROUND(({k})/3/0.5,0)*0.5)'
        return f'IF(({k})>=3,{frac(tb)}&" Tbsp",{frac("(" + k + ")")}&" tsp")'
    k = f'({k})'
    if unit == 'cup': return f'{frac(k)}&IF({k}<=1," cup"," cups")'
    return f'{frac(k)}&" {unit}"'
def cnt(q): return f'MAX(1,ROUND({q}*B3,0))'
def E(expr, base): return ('e', expr, base)          # expression part of a block, with its base-scale text

def ing_formula(d, metric_first=False):
    if d['kind'] == 'static': return d['text']
    if d['kind'] == 'count':
        k = cnt(d['q']); sc = f'{k}&" "&IF({k}=1,{Q(d["sing"])},{Q(d["plur"])})'
    else:
        a1 = amt(d['q'], d['unit']); a2 = amt(d['mq'], d['mu']) if d.get('mu') else None
        if metric_first and a2: a1, a2 = a2, a1
        sc = a1 + (f'&" ("&{a2}&")"' if a2 else '') + f'&" "&{Q(d["name"])}'
    return f'=IF(B3=1,{Q(d["base"])},{sc})'
def block_formula(parts):   # parts: literal strings and E(expr, base_text)
    base = ''.join(p if isinstance(p, str) else p[2] for p in parts)
    if all(isinstance(p, str) for p in parts): return base
    return f'=IF(B3=1,{Q(base)},' + '&'.join(Q(p) if isinstance(p, str) else p[1] for p in parts) + ')'

def split_long(text, n=130):   # Source Notes has no wrap: long lines continue on the next row
    out, line = [], ''
    for w in text.split(' '):
        if line and len(line) + 1 + len(w) > n: out.append(line); line = '   ' + w
        else: line = (line + ' ' + w) if line else w
    return out + [line]

def put(sh, ref, v, font, fill=None, border=None, al=None):
    c = sh[ref]; c.value = v; c.font = font
    if fill: c.fill = FILL(fill)
    if border: c.border = border
    if al: c.alignment = al
    return c

def add_photo(ws, path, credit, n, width_px=300):
    """Real dish photo only (never generated). Anchored at row 1, one blank column right of the table (G1 for 4 phases);
    about 300 px wide, aspect kept; credit caption (Arial 9 grey) just below the image's last row, same column."""
    from openpyxl.drawing.image import Image
    col = chr(66 + n + 1)                         # L + 2: leaves one empty column between table and photo
    img = Image(path); h = round(img.height * width_px / img.width); img.width, img.height = width_px, h
    ws.add_image(img, f'{col}1')
    ws.column_dimensions[col].width = 44           # ~300 px + margin, so the caption fits under the photo
    y, r = 0.0, 1                                  # walk row heights (pt -> px at 96 dpi; default row = 15 pt)
    while True:
        y += (ws.row_dimensions[r].height or 15) * 4 / 3
        if y >= h: break
        r += 1
    if credit: put(ws, f'{col}{r + 1}', credit, F(9, False, GREY))
    return col, r + 1

def build(R, out):
    ph = R['phases']; n = len(ph); L = chr(65 + n); cols = [chr(66 + i) for i in range(n)]
    t1 = R['tab1']; lab = R['label']                     # lab: "SERVINGS" or "BATCHES"
    assert len(t1) <= 31 and len(R['tab3']) <= 31, 'Excel tab names max 31 characters'
    wb = Workbook(); ws = wb.active; ws.title = t1
    ws.column_dimensions['A'].width = 48
    for i, c in enumerate(cols): ws.column_dimensions[c].width = 16 if i < 2 else 18
    put(ws, 'A1', R['title'], F(14, True, GREEN), CREAM, BOX, VCW); ws.row_dimensions[1].height = 27.75
    put(ws, 'A2', lab, F(11, True, GREEN), MINT, BOX); put(ws, 'B2', R['default'], F(14, True, BLUE), YEL, BOX, VC)
    put(ws, 'C2', R['note'], F(9, False, GREY), None, BOX, VC); ws.row_dimensions[2].height = 18
    put(ws, 'A3', 'Scale factor', F(10), CREAM, BOX); put(ws, 'B3', f'=B2/{R["base"]}', F(10, True), CREAM, BOX)
    put(ws, 'C3', f'=CONCATENATE("Currently scaled for ",B2," {R["unit_text"]}")', F(10), CREAM, BOX)
    ws.row_dimensions[4].height = 7.5
    for r, v in ((5, R['banner5']), (6, R['banner6'])):
        put(ws, f'A{r}', v, F(10, True), CREAM, BOX, VCW); ws.row_dimensions[r].height = 31.5
    put(ws, 'A7', 'INGREDIENT (auto-scales)', F(12, True, GREEN), MINT, BOX, VCW)
    for c, p in zip(cols, ph): put(ws, f'{c}7', p, F(12, True, GREEN), MINT, BOX, CCW)
    ws.row_dimensions[7].height = 21.75
    first = 8
    for i, d in enumerate(R['rows']):
        r = first + i
        put(ws, f'A{r}', ing_formula(d, R.get('metric_first', False)), F(12), CREAM, BOX, VCW)
        for c in cols: put(ws, f'{c}{r}', None, F(12, True), CREAM, BOX, CCW)
        ws.row_dimensions[r].height = d.get('h', 31)
    lastr = first + len(R['rows']) - 1
    merges = [f'A1:{L}1', f'C2:{L}2', f'C3:{L}3', f'A5:{L}5', f'A6:{L}6']
    for c, (i0, i1, parts) in R['blocks'].items():       # vertical phase blocks (row indexes into R['rows'])
        ws[f'{c}{first + i0}'].value = block_formula(parts)
        if i1 > i0: merges.append(f'{c}{first + i0}:{c}{first + i1}')
    sp = lastr + 1; ws.row_dimensions[sp].height = 9.75
    kt = sp + 1
    put(ws, f'A{kt}', R['keytips'], F(12, True, GREEN), MINT, None, VCW); ws.row_dimensions[kt].height = 24; merges.append(f'A{kt}:{L}{kt}')
    for j, t in enumerate(R['tips']):
        r = kt + 1 + j; put(ws, f'A{r}', '• ' + t, F(12), None, None, VCW); ws.row_dimensions[r].height = 18; merges.append(f'A{r}:{L}{r}')
    for m in merges: ws.merge_cells(m)          # openpyxl copies the top-left border onto the range edges
    ws.freeze_panes = 'A8'                      # gridlines stay ON, no print setup, default margins
    if R.get('photo'): add_photo(ws, R['photo'], R.get('photo_credit', ''), n)

    g = wb.create_sheet('Grocery List')
    for c, w in zip('ABC', (42, 55, 40)): g.column_dimensions[c].width = w
    put(g, 'A1', R['grocery_title'], F(14, True, GREEN), CREAM); g.merge_cells('A1:C1'); g.row_dimensions[1].height = 18
    put(g, 'A2', f'{lab.capitalize()} (linked to main sheet):', F(11)); put(g, 'B2', f"='{t1}'!B2", F(14, True, BLUE), YEL)
    put(g, 'A3', 'Scale factor:', F(11)); put(g, 'B3', f"='{t1}'!B3", F(11))
    g.row_dimensions[2].height = 18             # row 3 keeps the default height
    for c, h in zip('ABC', ('Item', 'Quantity (scaled)', 'Notes')): put(g, f'{c}5', h, F(12, True, GREEN), MINT, BOX)
    g.row_dimensions[5].height = 15.5
    items = R.get('grocery') or [(d['item'], ('row', i) if d['kind'] != 'static' else d.get('gq', ''), d.get('g', ''))
                                 for i, d in enumerate(R['rows'])]
    r = 6
    for item, q, note in items:
        qv = f"='{t1}'!A{first + q[1]}" if isinstance(q, tuple) else q
        for c, v in zip('ABC', (item, qv, note or None)): put(g, f'{c}{r}', v, F(10), None, BOX, VCW)
        g.row_dimensions[r].height = 30; r += 1
    r += 1                                   # one blank row, then the two footer lines
    for t in (R['howto'], R['baseline']):
        put(g, f'A{r}', t, F(9), None, None, WR); g.merge_cells(f'A{r}:C{r}'); g.row_dimensions[r].height = 24; r += 1

    s = wb.create_sheet(R['tab3']); s.column_dimensions['A'].width = 120
    put(s, 'A1', R['source_title'], F(14, True, GREEN), CREAM); s.row_dimensions[1].height = 18
    r = 2
    for ln in R['source_lines']:            # (bold, text) or None for a blank row
        if ln is None: r += 1; continue
        for part in split_long(ln[1]):
            put(s, f'A{r}', part, F(10, ln[0])); r += 1
    for sh in wb.worksheets:
        for row in sh.iter_rows():
            for c in row:
                if isinstance(c.value, str) and c.value.startswith('='): assert len(c.value) < 8000, c.coordinate
    wb.save(out)


def recalc(src, out):
    """Compute cached values with LibreOffice, then inject them into the openpyxl file (keeps its exact formatting;
    a LibreOffice-saved copy would change borders, row heights and page setup)."""
    import os, re, shutil, subprocess, tempfile, zipfile, openpyxl
    from xml.sax.saxutils import escape
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    subprocess.run(['soffice', '--headless', '--convert-to', 'xlsx', '--outdir', tmp, src], check=True, capture_output=True)
    vals = openpyxl.load_workbook(os.path.join(tmp, os.path.basename(src)), data_only=True)
    zin = zipfile.ZipFile(src); zout = zipfile.ZipFile(out + '.tmp', 'w', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED)
    for item in zin.infolist():
        data = zin.read(item.filename)
        m = re.match(r'xl/worksheets/sheet(\d+)\.xml$', item.filename)
        if m:
            ws = vals.worksheets[int(m.group(1)) - 1]
            def fill(mo):
                v = ws[mo.group(2)].value
                if v is None: v = ''
                if isinstance(v, bool): return f'{mo.group(1)} t="b">{mo.group(3)}<v>{int(v)}</v></c>'
                if isinstance(v, (int, float)): return f'{mo.group(1)}>{mo.group(3)}<v>{v}</v></c>'
                return f'{mo.group(1)} t="str">{mo.group(3)}<v>{escape(str(v))}</v></c>'
            data = re.sub(r'(<c r="([A-Z]+\d+)"(?: s="\d+")?)>(<f>.*?</f>)<v\s*/?>(?:</v>)?</c>', fill, data.decode('utf-8')).encode('utf-8')
        zout.writestr(item, data)
    zout.close(); shutil.move(out + '.tmp', out); shutil.rmtree(tmp)
```

## Google Sheets build path (native Sheet)
This path needs the Google Sheets and Google Drive connectors.
- **Setup:** create the sheet in the folder the owner chose (or the Drive root) with a descriptive name. Create the three tabs with the same names and order and write the values and formulas. Then format fills, fonts, merges (including the vertical phase blocks), borders, column widths and row heights. Freeze 7 rows on the Recipe Table.
- **Widths:** pixels are about 7 per character plus 5:
  - Recipe Table: A 48 → 341 px, 16 → 117 px, 18 → 131 px.
  - Grocery List: 42 → 299 px, 55 → 390 px, 40 → 285 px.
  - Source Notes: 120 → 845 px.
- **Row heights:** points × 1.333 = pixels. 27.75 → 37, 18 → 24, 7.5 → 10, 31.5 → 42, 21.75 → 29, 31 → 41, 9.75 → 13, 24 → 32, 15.5 → 21, 30 → 40. Leave default rows (Recipe Table row 3, Grocery List rows 3–4, Source Notes rows 2+) unset.
- **Borders:** thin black (`#000000`) solid on all four sides of the bordered cells. Apply the border to the whole merged range (Sheets draws a merge's outline from the range).
- **What already matches:** gridlines are on and there is no print setup, which is Sheets' default. No hidden columns are needed because the math is inline.
- **Connector limits:** the connector cannot set print setup, zoom or tab colors, none of which this format needs. If a Source Notes line overflows into column B in Sheets, that's the same no-wrap behavior as Excel.
- **Formulas:** `IF`, `ROUND`, `INT`, `MAX`, `CHOOSE`, `ROUNDUP`, `CONCATENATE`, `CHAR(10)`, `&` and `'Tab Name'!A1` references all work. Quote tab names that contain spaces or the en dash. Turn on wrap for the phase blocks so `CHAR(10)` breaks show.
- **Verify** by reading every tab back with no `#REF!`, `#NAME?` or `#VALUE!`. Test scaling by changing B2, reading back column A, a phase block and the Grocery List, then set B2 back to the base value.
- **Source Notes:** the rating, links and original text all go on the Source Notes tab, as in the Excel version.
- **Dish photo:** if the photo has a public URL, put `=IMAGE("<url>")` in the photo column cell at row 1, merge that cell down over the rows the image needs (or set the row height), and add the caption cell below as in Excel. If only a local file exists, insert it as an over-grid image through the Sheets UI if available; the connectors cannot upload an over-grid image, so otherwise leave the photo out and say so in Source Notes.
